about.metaDescription: How OpenDock scores OpenCode plugins, what the health marks mean, and how to get a plugin listed or corrected.
about.title: About OpenDock
about.lead: OpenDock lists every OpenCode plugin published on npm and ranks them by how much they are really used. It is independent and not affiliated with OpenCode. Data is refreshed daily from public npm and GitHub data, and nobody can pay for a position.
about.rankingIntro: Every plugin gets a score from 0 to 100 from four signals:

signals.downloads: npm downloads in the last month. The clearest sign that people actually install it.
signals.stars: GitHub stars, capped by downloads, so a plugin inside a famous repository does not borrow that repository’s fame.
signals.activity: Days since the last push. Full marks within a week, fading to zero after a year.
signals.momentum: Stars gained in the last 30 days, relative to size, so new plugins can climb.

about.archived: An archived repository keeps about a third of its score.

healthBody.ok: Recent activity, with a source repository, README and license.
healthBody.warn: No update in six months, or no linked repository, README or license.
healthBody.danger: Archived, deprecated on npm, or no update in over a year.

about.listBody: Add the <keyword></keyword> keyword to your package.json and publish to npm. Your plugin appears after the next daily refresh. No form, no pull request. A description, repository link, README and license improve your health mark and how well search finds you.
about.fixBody: Categories are assigned automatically and can be wrong. Corrections to the category, description or repository go through a reviewed override file.
about.removeBody: Drop the <keyword></keyword> keyword, or open an issue asking to be blocklisted. The next refresh removes it.
